issues.description: Breaking rename of public RequestMetadataFrame without deprecation alias
issues.detail: RequestMetadataFrame is removed outright from pipecat.frames.frames and replaced with ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame. External code importing the old name will fail at import time. Keep a deprecation alias (RequestMetadataFrame = ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame) emitting DeprecationWarning for at least one release.

issues.description: ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame leaks downstream past switcher and non-switcher pipelines
issues.detail: push_frame only suppresses the frame when frame.service == active_service, so stale or non-active targets escape downstream. Combined with STTService now pushing the frame downstream after handling, an STT used outside a ServiceSwitcher leaks this internal control frame into the pipeline. Always consume the frame at the switcher boundary.

issues.description: service field has no default and uses unresolved forward-reference string for FrameProcessor
issues.detail: The required `service: "FrameProcessor"` field breaks any external zero-arg constructors with TypeError, and FrameProcessor is not imported (even under TYPE_CHECKING) in frames.py. get_type_hints() and serializer tooling will fail to resolve it. Add a TYPE_CHECKING import and consider a default of None for backward compatibility.

issues.description: Embedding live FrameProcessor reference in a Frame creates structural and equality hazards
issues.detail: Frames are data-only dataclasses; storing a live processor handle risks cycles, repr/serialization blowups, and dataclass-generated __eq__/__hash__ comparing processors structurally. Prefer storing a stable service name/id and resolving in the switcher, or mark the field with compare=False and document the contract.

issues.description: Service comparison uses == instead of identity check `is`
issues.detail: `frame.service == self.strategy.active_service` relies on default equality. If FrameProcessor or a subclass ever overrides __eq__ (or dataclass-generated equality kicks in), two distinct services could compare equal and the wrong frame would be consumed. Use `is` for instance identity, matching intent.

issues.description: No test asserts frame suppression at switcher boundary or non-active-service path
issues.detail: Tests verify the targeted service receives the frame but never assert ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame is consumed at the ServiceSwitcher boundary, nor cover the non-active-service targeting branch. Add a regression test locking in suppression behavior and exercising both branches of the new conditional.

synthesis.summary: The panel unanimously flags the rename as a breaking public API change with no deprecation alias, the required `service` field's missing default and unresolved forward-reference type, and a leakage problem where the internal control frame now escapes past the switcher (and outside switcher contexts via STTService) when frame.service doesn't match the active service. Embedding a live FrameProcessor inside a dataclass Frame is also a structural smell that affects equality, serialization, and lifecycle. The == comparison should be `is`, and test coverage should lock in suppression at the switcher boundary. The refactor is mechanically clean but the contract needs tightening before merge.
